scenes.visual: Title card: Radial Glia Make Cortical Neurons. Show a blue radial glial cell and a green neuron beside its fibre.

scenes.tts: In embryonic rodent cortex, radial glia make most cortical neurons. The cells that guide migrating neurons are also their main source. That changes how we see the scaffold. A radial glial cell is a progenitor, a cell that still divides. Its daughters can become neurons while it keeps making more.

scenes.visual: Open on a blue radial glial cell spanning the cortical wall, with a green neuron migrating along its fibre. Label the two roles: main cortical progenitor and migration scaffold. Show a division leaving a blue radial glial daughter and a green neuron. Keep the main finding on screen.

scenes.tts: How do we know? In mouse, sorted radial glia made neurons in culture. Fate mapping marked their descendants. Nearly all cortical projection neurons carried the mark. In filmed rat slices, radial glia divided and made neurons that moved along the parent's own fiber. Dye-filled recordings also tied dividing precursors to radial glial shape.

scenes.visual: Show three evidence panels, labelled mouse sorting and fate mapping, rat lineage imaging, and rat recording and dye filling. In the mouse panel distinguish neurons made in culture from permanently marked projection-neuron descendants in the animal. In the rat film panel show a division and the neuronal daughter following the parent fibre. In the recording panel reveal the filled precursor's radial glial shape.

scenes.tts: There are two routes to a neuron. Direct neurogenesis makes another radial glial cell and a neuron. Indirect neurogenesis makes another radial glial cell and an intermediate progenitor. That progenitor leaves the ventricle and divides in the subventricular zone, usually into two neurons in rodents. This adds neurons without spending the radial glial cell. Human cortex also has many outer radial glia, which feed further progenitors.

scenes.visual: Show side-by-side ancestry trees: radial glia to radial glia plus neuron; radial glia to radial glia plus intermediate progenitor, then usually two neurons. Label these rodent example lineages, with variable intermediate-progenitor yields. Show the intermediate progenitor losing ventricular contact and dividing in the SVZ. Finish with a small human-cortex inset showing outer radial glia away from the ventricle feeding further progenitors. Do not imply fixed route frequencies.

scenes.tts: These progenitors touch two niches, local settings that help keep a stem cell a stem cell. The apical foot faces cerebrospinal fluid. In mouse, growth factors in that fluid support proliferation. The basal foot rests on basement membrane under the pia. A daughter that leaves loses apical contact.

scenes.tts: Neuron output also depends on how many daughters keep dividing. Call that fraction P, and the fraction that quits Q. P plus Q equals one. Below Q equals zero point five, the pool grows. At zero point five, it holds steady. Above it, it shrinks. An intermediate progenitor still counts in P. In mouse cortex, the cell cycle lengthens, mostly in G one.

scenes.visual: Show P as daughters remaining progenitors and Q as daughters exiting the cycle, with P + Q = 1. Animate a growing pool for Q < 0.5, a steady pool for Q = 0.5, and a shrinking pool for Q > 0.5. Count intermediate progenitors in P. Finish with a mouse cell-cycle ring whose G1 segment lengthens; do not depict G1 duration alone determining fate.

scenes.tts: Inside an apical progenitor, the nucleus moves with that cycle. Picture a lift. The shaft is the cell; the car is the nucleus. In G one, it moves basally. S phase copies DNA in the basal ventricular zone. In G two, it returns apically. Mitosis happens there. Nuclei at different heights make a single cell layer look layered.

scenes.visual: Show nuclei at different heights within a single layer of elongated apical progenitors, labelled pseudostratified. Zoom to one cell and retain the lift analogy. Synchronize its nucleus with a G1/S/G2/M ring: basal movement in G1, DNA copying in basal VZ during S, apical return in G2, apical mitosis. Show no motor assignments.
